column20: What went wrong and why? - "a fiber cut caused by severe weather conditions in the Netherlands"; V1b from "These links were already running at higher utilization than our design target"
column21: What went wrong and why? - "25% of network links between two campuses of West Europe datacenters became unavailable"
column22: What happened? - "impacted network traffic between Availability Zones within the West Europe region"; region-scoped, see "impacted a single region"
column23: How can customers make incidents like this less impactful? - "incidents like this one that impacted a single region"
column24: What happened? - "one of the four major paths was cut"; other three paths stayed up, impact came from "traffic on the remaining links exceeded their capacity", so redundancy did not fail together
column25: How did we respond? - "At 10:00 UTC we initiated throttling and migration of internal service traffic away from the region"; impact only ended "by 16:00 UTC" after manual simulations and rebalancing
column26: How did we respond? - mitigation was manual network engineering work: "Our networking on-call engineers engaged and began to investigate"; no central controller or bad config push is described
column27: How can customers make incidents like this less impactful? - "Customers should consider a multi-region geodiversity strategy ... to avoid impact from incidents like this one that impacted a single region"; no statement on isolated tenants or a pre-tested local fallback
column28: V9 uses the stated customer impact window 07:22-16:00 UTC (later milestones: link full restoration 20:50, mitigated declared 22:45); V8b coded yes from the advisory multi-region guidance
